newsitem.title: CHINA: China to limit new petrochemical, ethylene plants.
newsitem.headline: China to limit new petrochemical, ethylene plants.

text.p: China will restrict the construction of new oil refining projects and ethylene production plants until the year 2000, the official China Daily said on Wednesday.
China would improve and expand existing refineries instead of setting up new projects, the newspaper said.

Restricting the construction of new petrochemical and ethylene plants would help curb the creation of redundant projects, the China Daily quoted Ma Chengquan, a senior official of the State Planning Commission, as saying.

Beginning immediately all foreign or domestically funded projects to create or expand crude oil processing plants must be first checked by the State Planning Commission before being submitted for approval by the State Council, or cabinet, it said.
Beijing would not allow new ethylene production plants before 2000, except for those foreign funded projects already approved, it said but gave no details.
Existing refineries and those under construction would be capable of satisfying China's soaring demand for crude oil processing by 2000, said the State Planning Commissions's Ma.
The government would launch an overhaul of existing crude oil processing projects and would issue licences to those considered qualified, China Daily quoted him as saying.
Those without licences would be barred from crude oil processing, he said.
Increasing oil imports from the Middle East were unavoidable, because China's domestic production was unlikely to meet the needs of its economic development, he said.
China would improve and expand existing ethylene plants and would encourage multi-channel funding and joint investment by different areas and government departments, Ma said.
The Securities Daily said some enterprises would be allowed to issue convertible bonds or to adjust their assets to raise funds for ethylene projects.
Neither newspaper gave details on the status of refinery and ethylene projects currently under discussion with foreign companies.

Dow Chemical Co on Monday signed a letter of intent with China Petrochemical Corp (Sinopec) for a multi-billion dollar petrochemical complex that would have annual capacity of up to 600,000 tonnes of ethylene.
Dow officials said they hoped construction on the first phase of the project would begin in 2000, but gave no specific date for completion.
